title: The Warship That Sank in Minutes (1628)

segments.vo: Sweden's mightiest warship sank minutes into her first voyage.
This really happened.
Stockholm, August tenth, sixteen twenty-eight.

scenes.sub: BUILT FOR KING GUSTAV II ADOLF

segments.vo: The ship was called the Vasa, and she was built for King Gustav the Second Adolf of Sweden.
segments.cap: The ship was called the Vasa, and she was built for King Gustav II Adolf of Sweden.

segments.vo: She carried sixty-four guns on two gun decks.
segments.cap: She carried 64 guns on two gun decks.

segments.vo: Before she sailed, thirty men ran back and forth across her deck.
segments.cap: Before she sailed, 30 men ran back and forth across her deck.

segments.vo: After just three runs, she rolled so badly the test was stopped.
segments.cap: After just 3 runs, she rolled so badly the test was stopped.

segments.vo: Under pressure, she was sent to sea anyway.
segments.cap: Under pressure, she was sent to sea anyway.

segments.vo: She left the dock in Stockholm and managed only thirteen hundred metres.
segments.cap: She left the dock in Stockholm and managed only 1,300 metres.

segments.vo: Then she leaned over, water rushed in, and she went down.
segments.cap: Then she leaned over, water rushed in, and she went down.

segments.vo: She settled thirty-two metres down, right in the harbour.
segments.cap: She settled 32 metres down, right in the harbour.

segments.vo: About thirty people died.
The captain was arrested.
But in the end, nobody was ever punished.
segments.cap: But in the end, nobody was ever punished.

segments.vo: But the strangest part came centuries later.
segments.cap: But the strangest part came centuries later.

segments.vo: Then, in nineteen fifty-six, an explorer named Anders Fran-zen found the wreck.
segments.cap: Then, in 1956, an explorer named Anders Franzén found the wreck.

segments.vo: In April nineteen sixty-one, after three hundred and thirty-three years, she broke the surface.
segments.cap: In April 1961, after 333 years, she broke the surface.

segments.vo: And she was still ninety-eight percent original.
The cold, brackish Baltic had kept the wood-eating shipworms away, so her timbers survived.
segments.cap: The cold, brackish Baltic had kept the wood-eating shipworms away, so her timbers survived.
